We’ve seen reports Japan sent a memo to the government last month suggesting they did not believe the prime minister’s comments about the pair of crown melons he received as a gift were made with “ill intention”. This is one of our most important partnerships. This is a national embarrassment. Now, we can say, ‘yes, but, you know, some people think it isn’t.’ Well, here we are on national radio talking about it. The Australian prime minister has been inappropriate … I’m the shadow minister for foreign affairs. I don’t have the authority to apologise on behalf of the government or the prime minister. If I did have that authority, I would have done so. People who want to have a punt should be allowed to have a punt. But we should also recognise it comes with harmful effects that need to be addressed … we’ve got to protect children from being exposed unnecessarily to gambling ads when really they should be spending time with family. title.en: PM asks justice secretary to find way to exclude PC Harper’s killers from early release scheme
title.zh: 首相要求司法大臣将杀害警员哈珀的凶手排除在提前释放计划之外

summary.en: The UK Prime Minister has instructed the justice secretary to explore options for excluding the killers of PC Andrew Harper from a prison early release scheme. This directive follows increasing pressure from the victim's family and police, with the scheme originally intended to alleviate prison overcrowding.
summary.zh: 英国首相已指示司法大臣，研究如何将杀害警员安德鲁·哈珀的凶手排除在旨在缓解监狱拥挤的提前释放计划之外。此举是在受害者家属和警方日益增长的压力下作出的。

body.en: Andy Burnham said to be ‘determined’ to work out solution after increasing pressure from family and police Andy Burnham has told the justice secretary to find a way to exclude PC Andrew Harper’s killers from the early release scheme aimed at easing prison overcrowding. The prime minister is said to be “determined” that a solution can be found after increasing pressure from Harper’s family and police not to allow Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter, to be freed in January under the existing plans. Continue reading...
body.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 表示，在来自家人和警方的压力越来越大后，他“决心”找到解决方案 安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 告诉司法部长，想办法将杀害安德鲁·哈珀 (PC Andrew Harper) 的凶手排除在旨在缓解监狱人满为患的提前释放计划之外。据称，在哈珀家人和警方施加越来越大的压力后，总理“决心”找到解决方案，不允许根据现有计划于 1 月份释放因过失杀人罪被判处 13 年徒刑的杰西·科尔 (Jessie Cole) 和阿尔伯特·鲍尔斯 (Albert Bowers)。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This situation highlights the solemn responsibility of leaders to uphold justice and righteousness, especially when innocent lives are taken. Yahweh's call to rulers is to ensure that justice is done and that the vulnerable are protected, reflecting a deep concern for societal order and accountability.
reflection.zh: 这一事件凸显了领导者维护公义和正直的庄严责任，尤其是在无辜生命被夺走的情况下。雅伟呼召统治者确保伸张正义，保护弱者，这反映了对社会秩序和问责制的深切关注。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Overnight Russian strikes on Ukraine used North Korean missiles, claims Zelenskyy – Europe live
title.zh: 泽连斯基称俄罗斯对乌克兰的夜间袭击使用了朝鲜导弹——欧洲直播

summary.en: Russian forces launched overnight missile attacks on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, resulting in at least six fatalities and 20 injuries, according to officials. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy claimed that North Korean missiles were used in these strikes.
summary.zh: 官员称，俄罗斯军队对乌克兰扎波罗热市发动了夜间导弹袭击，造成至少六人死亡、20人受伤。乌克兰总统泽连斯基声称，这些袭击使用了朝鲜导弹。

body.en: Russian attacks on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed at least six people and injured 20, officials said Overnight Russian attacks on the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed at least six people and injured 20, officials said. Another six people were killed and 16 injured in attacks on Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk , Reuters reported. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Zaporizhzhia “was struck with North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons, and guided aerial bombs.” “Every step Russia takes – increasing ballistic missile production, bringing in North Korean equipment, preparing for mobilisation – all of this shows that Moscow is preparing not for peace, but for escalation. And the world needs to respond now, not wait.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 官员称，俄罗斯对乌克兰城市扎波罗热的袭击造成至少 6 人死亡、20 人受伤，官员称，隔夜俄罗斯对乌克兰东南部城市扎波罗热的袭击造成至少 6 人死亡、20 人受伤。据路透社报道，第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克和顿涅茨克的袭击另有 6 人死亡、16 人受伤。乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基表示，扎波罗热“遭到朝鲜弹道导弹、锆石和制导航空炸弹的袭击”。 “俄罗斯采取的每一步——增加弹道导弹产量、引进朝鲜装备、准备动员——所有这一切都表明，莫斯科不是在为和平做准备，而是在为升级做准备。世界需要立即做出反应，而不是等待。”继续阅读...

Yet, the Scriptures remind us that Yahweh's steadfast love and mercies are new every morning, offering a source of enduring faithfulness even amidst the deepest sorrow. This promise encourages us to look for His sustaining grace each day, even when...
reflection.zh: 面对持续的冲突所带来的破坏和损失，人们可能难以找到希望。然而，圣经提醒我们，雅伟的坚定之爱和怜悯每早晨都是新的，即使在最深的悲痛中，也提供了一个持久信实的源泉。这个应许鼓励我们每天寻求祂的持续恩典，即便环境看起来黯淡无光。

verse.textEn: Because of Yahweh's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.

title.en: Amber heat health alerts to kick in across England ahead of fifth summer heatwave – latest news
title.zh: 英格兰将发布琥珀色高温健康警报，迎来夏季第五波热浪——最新消息

summary.en: England is facing its fifth summer heatwave, with amber heat health alerts issued across most of the country. This comes after 11 regions were officially declared to be in drought.
summary.zh: 英格兰大部分地区已发布琥珀色高温健康警报，预计将迎来夏季第五波热浪。此前，该国已有11个地区正式宣布进入干旱状态。

body.en: The alerts come a day after it was officially declared that there are now 11 regions in the country in drought As we mentioned in the opening post , amber heat health alerts come into force across most of England from 9am today and will last until 9am on Friday. As well as a rise in deaths and likely “significant” impacts across health and social care services, here are some of the other risks associated with the amber category, as outlined by the UK Health Security Agency: internal temperatures in hospitals and care homes may exceed the recommended threshold for clinical risk assessment the heat affecting the ability of the workforce to deliver services indoor environments overheating increasing the risk to some vulnerable people issues managing medicines increased demand for power exceeding capacity possible travel delays water‑related incidents may increase, including risks from cold‑water shock and drowning Continue reading...
body.zh: 在正式宣布该国目前有 11 个地区处于干旱状态的前一天，正如我们在开篇文章中提到的，琥珀色高温健康警报从今天上午 9 点开始在英格兰大部分地区生效，并将持续到周五上午 9 点。除了死亡人数上升以及可能对健康和社会护理服务产生“重大”影响外，英国卫生安全局概述了与琥珀类别相关的一些其他风险： 医院和疗养院的内部温度可能超过临床风险评估的建议阈值 热量影响劳动力提供服务的能力 室内环境过热增加了某些弱势群体的风险 药物管理问题 对电力的需求增加超过容量 可能的旅行延误 与水有关的事件可能会增加，包括冷水冲击和溺水的风险继续阅读...

reflection.en: The widespread heat alerts and declared drought in England remind us of the strain on our natural world. Yahweh's creation, though resilient, often groans under the weight of environmental changes, prompting us to reflect on our role and responsibility. Even amidst these challenges, we are called to hope and diligent stewardship.
reflection.zh: 英格兰大范围的高温警报和宣布的干旱，提醒我们自然世界所承受的压力。雅伟的创造，尽管具有韧性，却常在环境变化的重压下发出呻吟，促使我们反思自己的角色和责任。即使面对这些挑战，我们仍被呼召要心怀希望并勤勉地管理受托之物。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Thousands of hectares burnt as El Niño intensifies Indonesia's dry season
title.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象加剧印尼旱季，数千公顷土地被烧毁

summary.en: Wildfires in Indonesia have consumed thousands of hectares this year, an area double that of 2023, which was one of the hottest years on record, intensified by the El Niño weather pattern.
summary.zh: 今年印尼的野火已烧毁数千公顷土地，是2023年（有记录以来最热的年份之一）烧毁面积的两倍，这主要是由厄尔尼诺天气模式加剧的。

body.en:
Dozens of Indonesian schools were shut for a second day on Tuesday as forest fires continued to burn during an intense dry season expected to be worsened by El Niño.

In West Kalimantan on the island of Borneo that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, the mayor of the capital Pontianak ordered schools closed due to the smoke wafting over the city from fires elsewhere.

Public records show Pontianak, with a population of around 660,000 people, has tens of thousands of public school pupils.

Children will learn from home for as long as air quality remains poor, mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono said in a statement, without stating how many schools were affected.

"We have started to feel it, especially at night and in the morning, as haze has already blanketed the city of Pontianak," he said.

On the island of Java, firefighters battled flames for a ninth day at a national park that has lost 900 hectares to an inferno that broke out on Monday last week.

The blaze at the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, a major tourist attraction closed to visitors since Saturday, is one of several fires that have drawn in nearly 50,000 firefighters countrywide.

Indonesia is forecast to experience an unusually tough dry season this year with a high risk for drought and wildfires due in part to the El Niño weather phenomenon, the BMKG weather agency has said.

The fire at the Bromo park in East Java has consumed nearly 900 hectares by Tuesday morning.

This is equivalent to over 1,200 football fields and nearly 2 per cent of the total park area.

"We’re making our best effort and mobilising everything ... to extinguish and wet-down the area," local disaster official Satriyo Nurseno said.

"We hope that today we can put out the fire in all areas, then carry out soaking so that the fire does not reignite."

Three water-bombing helicopters and fire trucks were providing support to about 200 firefighters, forest rangers, police and soldiers helping to put out the blaze.

According to the BNPB disaster agency, more than 48,000 personnel have been deployed to fight fires in six provinces.

Security minister Djamari Chaniago said on Monday Indonesia has deployed 43 helicopters and up to 15 fixed-wing planes for cloud seeding where needed.

The process involves spraying particles such as silver iodide and salt from aircraft to produce rainfall, but depends on clouds being present.

As Indonesia braces for the worst effects of El Niño, the BMKG said the average air temperature in July was 27C — higher than the 26.2C average.

title.en: At least 132 killed in Colombia's largest earthquake in years
title.zh: 哥伦比亚发生多年来最大地震，至少132人死亡

summary.en: A powerful earthquake in Colombia has resulted in at least 132 fatalities and over 480 injuries, with fears that more individuals remain trapped under collapsed structures.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚发生强烈地震，造成至少132人死亡，超过480人受伤，预计仍有更多人被困在倒塌的建筑物下。

body.en:
At least 132 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.

The death toll is likely to rise, with more feared trapped under collapsed buildings.

The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) at a depth of 103km (64 miles) in Chocó province, the country's geological service said. It was felt across an enormous area, stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia.

Many of the deaths have been concentrated in the city of Pereira, in Colombia's coffee-growing region, with surrounding cities and the Valle del Cauca region also hit hard.

The epicentre of the quake was near the village of San José del Palmar, in Chocó province, but local mayor León Fabio Marín Moncada said that there had miraculously been no deaths or injuries - despite the roads in and out being damaged.

More than 480 people were injured in the quakes, Colombia's Association of Capital Cities wrote in a statement update on Monday.

About 55km (34 miles) from the epicentre of the earthquake, the city of Pereira saw some of the worst damage.

Videos verified by the BBC show at least one building collapsing in Plaza Bolívar, the city's main square, with scattered debris and dust across the open space where many people had gathered.

Local authorities have reported at least 40 people dead in the city's metropolitan area, with 65 collapsed buildings. People are believed to be trapped in 15 of them.

A curfew is in place in some parts of the city until 05:00 local time on Tuesday.

Thirty-two buildings collapsed in Cali, located about 160km south of Pereira and about 200km from the epicentre.

Dan Cutler, 29, is from London but has been in Colombia for about two months as part of a big trip with his partner, and is currently in Cali.

Being woken by the earthquake, he told the BBC: "I've never experienced anything like it."

"We sprinted outside in our pyjamas. There's no major structural damage to the hotel, but there are surface cracks in the walls, and paint and plaster have peeled off," he says.

There were also reports of deaths in Manizales, Quibdó, Medellín, across the Chocó and Valle del Cauca regions.

Speaking to BBC World Service, Angélica Ávila said she had been staying in a hotel in Manizales.

"Everyone was screaming... I saw dust coming out of the neighbouring buildings, and bricks were falling off the walls," she said.

Journalist and meteorologist Luis Felipe Molina, from Manizales, was at home when the earthquake struck - about 150km from the epicentre.

He explained that due to previous earthquakes, the city has "very strict seismic-resistant building regulations" - so his building was able to resist the impact.

reflection.en: In the wake of such devastating natural disasters, where lives are lost and communities are shattered, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength. For those facing immense loss and uncertainty, this verse offers a profound source of comfort and a reminder of divine presence in times of deepest trouble.
reflection.zh: 在如此毁灭性的自然灾害之后，生命逝去，社区破碎，诗篇46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量。对于那些面临巨大损失和不确定性的人来说，这节经文在最深的困境中提供了深刻的安慰和对神同在的提醒。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.

title.en: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
title.zh: 特朗普签署行政命令限制和分拆儿童疫苗

summary.en: The Trump administration has signed an order to limit and split childhood vaccines, continuing its promotion of a discredited link between vaccines and autism.
summary.zh: 特朗普政府签署了一项限制和分拆儿童疫苗的行政命令，此前该政府长期以来一直推动疫苗与自闭症之间已被证实的虚假关联。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has signed an order that calls for fewer childhood vaccines and also recommends splitting the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) shots.

"Decades ago, children received only a small fraction of the vaccines required today," Trump said. "In those times, people were much healthier and of course the high rates of autism now observed did not exist."

The president has long cast doubt on the safety of MMR vaccines, but multiple studies have found no connection between the shots and autism.

The order also recommends that the number of childhood vaccines drop to 11 from the existing 18 recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).

Trump's order serves as guidance, not a mandate, since shots required for school attendance are set at the state level, rather than by the federal government.

Speaking in the Oval Office on Monday, the president said his administration "is recognising gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases".

The immunisations recommended for all children under the order are for measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type B, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus, and varicella or chicken pox.

"We're reducing them," Trump said. "It's not only that you're doing fewer vaccines, or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor."

The president suggested the MMR vaccine could be "quite lethal" if given at once. He compared it to pouring a bottle of soda into a child's body.

When a reporter asked for evidence of the "lethal" claim, Trump said: "What I've heard is that there are some people that say it is that way."

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) , external , the MMR vaccine carries a very small risk of febrile seizures for young children. Those with health issues, including severe allegeric reactions or weakened immune systems, are advised to consult with healthcare providers before taking the shots.

The agency says "most people who get MMR vaccine do not have any serious problems with it", and that getting the vaccine "is much safer than getting measles, mumps, or rubella".

According to the CDC, there is "no published scientific evidence that shows any benefit in separating the combination MMR vaccine into three individual shots".

Experts say that allowing time between jabs means children are more likely to contract diseases in the interim or that they are more likely to miss appointments if there are multiple shots.

Trump's Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F Kennedy Jr said the proposed changes were meant to give parents choice, not prohibit access to childhood vaccines.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普签署了一项命令，要求减少儿童疫苗接种，并建议将腮腺炎、麻疹和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗分为三针。 特朗普周一表示：“几十年前，儿童只接种了当今所需疫苗的一小部分。” “在那个时代，人们更加健康，当然，现在观察到的高自闭症发病率并不存在。” 特朗普政府长期以来一直在推动疫苗与自闭症之间的不可信联系。

reflection.en: In a world grappling with complex health decisions, the call to speak truth and put away falsehood remains vital. When policies are shaped by discredited claims, it underscores the importance of seeking and upholding verifiable information for the well-being of all, especially the most vulnerable.
reflection.zh: 在一个面临复杂健康决策的世界里，说真话、弃绝谎言的呼召至关重要。当政策被已被证实的虚假主张所左右时，这突显了寻求和维护可验证信息的重要性，以保障所有人的福祉，特别是那些最脆弱的群体。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: Young girl finds whale stranded on Australian beach
title.zh: 小女孩在澳大利亚海滩发现搁浅鲸鱼

summary.en: A young girl discovered a humpback whale stranded on an Australian beach. The whale was later able to free itself as the tide rose in Queensland, Australia.
summary.zh: 一名小女孩在澳大利亚海滩上发现了一头搁浅的座头鲸。随后，随着潮水上涨，这头鲸鱼成功地自行脱困。

body.en:
A young girl and her mother found a humpback whale stranded at Wathumba Creek in K'gari, Queensland, Australia.

The whale later self-released on the afternoon of Sunday 9 August, according to the Queensland Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation.

It advises not to touch, interfere with or get close to stranded marine animals and to report them immediately.
body.zh: 一名小女孩和她的母亲在澳大利亚昆士兰州卡加里的瓦桑巴溪发现了一头搁浅的座头鲸。 据昆士兰州环境、旅游、科学和创新部称，这头鲸鱼后来于 8 月 9 日星期日下午自行释放。 建议不要触摸、干扰或接近搁浅的海洋动物，并立即报告。

reflection.en: This story of a stranded whale finding freedom as the tide rises reminds us that even in moments of distress, relief can come with the turning of the natural world. It echoes the truth that difficult seasons, like a long night, often give way to unexpected joy and liberation. Yahweh's timing can bring about a hopeful reversal.
reflection.zh: 这头搁浅的鲸鱼随着潮水上涨而重获自由的故事提醒我们，即使在困境中，随着自然界的转变，解脱也会到来。它呼应了一个真理：艰难的季节，如同漫长的黑夜，常常会迎来意想不到的喜乐和释放。雅伟的时刻能带来充满希望的转机。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: Trump pushes overhaul of US policy on vaccines for children
title.zh: 特朗普推动改革美国儿童疫苗政策

summary.en: In an executive order, President Trump calls for fewer recommended childhood vaccinations and more spacing between shots. Medical experts say the changes lack scientific backing and could leave children less protected.
summary.zh: 特朗普总统在一项行政命令中呼吁减少建议的儿童疫苗接种，并延长接种间隔。医学专家表示，这些改变缺乏科学依据，可能导致儿童保护不足。

body.en:
In an executive order, President Trump calls for fewer recommended childhood vaccinations and more spacing between shots. Medical experts say the changes lack scientific backing and could leave children less protected.

On Monday, President Donald Trump signed an executive order seeking sweeping changes to the US's childhood vaccine policy, including fewer recommended immunizations and more separate appointments for children to receive them.

The order calls for the combined measles , mumps and rubella vaccine, known as MMR, to be separated into three single-disease shots. It also advocates administering childhood immunizations at separate medical visits whenever possible.

Trump described the move as a "major victory for parents rights, religious and constitutional rights, and for the gold standard science."

The order says the federal government will support 11 core childhood vaccinations and advises states and territories to review vaccine requirements for school enrollment.

However, Washington cannot directly determine most school vaccine mandates, which are largely set by individual states. On those requirements, Trump's order is therefore primarily a recommendation.

The order also directs the Health and Human Services Department to improve vaccine research and develop a plan to make separate measles, mumps and rubella vaccines available in the US. Such single-antigen vaccines are not currently licensed there.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. had already sought in January to remove vaccines against six of 17 diseases from the childhood schedule. A federal judge later blocked those changes while legal proceedings continue. Monday's order reaffirms much of that overhaul.

Public health experts say childhood vaccination schedules are based on extensive research into when and how vaccines can safely be administered together. Safety monitoring continues after vaccines are introduced.

They warn that spreading shots across more appointments can leave children vulnerable to preventable diseases for longer and increase the risk that later doses are delayed or missed.

Vaccine maker Merck said there was no published scientific evidence showing any benefit from splitting the MMR vaccine. Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, estimated that developing and approving separate vaccines in the US could take more than a decade.

"We're advising that you continue to give children a vaccine that has decades of safety data," said Aaron M. Milstone, a member of the AAP Committee on Infectious Diseases.

Speaking in the Oval Office, Trump repeatedly suggested that the number or timing of childhood vaccines could be linked to rising rates of autism spectrum disorder.

reflection.en: Leaders bear a weighty responsibility to seek and heed sound counsel, especially when decisions impact public health and the well-being of the most vulnerable. The wisdom found in a multitude of experts can provide safety and prevent unintended harm. May all those in authority be guided by discernment and a commitment to the common good.
reflection.zh: 领袖肩负重任，尤其当决策影响公众健康和最脆弱群体的福祉时，更应寻求并听取明智的建议。众多的专家智慧能带来安全，避免不必要的伤害。愿所有掌权者都以明辨的心和对公共利益的承诺为指引。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Jackie, the famous California bald eagle, dies after weeks of intensive care
title.zh: 加州著名白头海雕杰基在数周重症监护后去世

summary.en: Jackie, a renowned bald eagle from California, has passed away after receiving intensive care for several weeks. She and her mate, Shadow, had been observed by millions globally through the Big Bear Eagle Nest Cam.
summary.zh: 加州著名的白头海雕杰基在接受数周的重症监护后去世。杰基和她的伴侣沙多多年来通过大熊湖鹰巢摄像头被数百万人关注。

body.en:
Jackie, a bald eagle in California who became an online star, died on Monday after receiving weeks of veterinary treatment.

Jackie was being cared for by Ojai Raptor Center, a wildlife rehabilitation organisation, after she was attacked by other eagles. The bird had underlying health issues that caused anaemia and weight loss.

"Over the past several days, her condition continued to deteriorate despite intensive treatment and the combined efforts of our veterinary team and consulting specialists," Ojai Raptor Center said in a statement.

A livestream featuring the Big Bear Valley nest of Jackie and her partner, Shadow, has hundreds of thousands of subscribers.

The Big Bear Eagle Nest Cam, run by the nonprofit Friends of Big Bear Valley in California, amassed a loyal following and Jackie was frequently spotted in the area since she hatched in the spring of 2012.

Jackie and Shadow had been mates since 2018, the Friends of Big Bear Valley website said.

"Our team is heartbroken. It has been an extraordinary privilege to care for her," the Ojai Raptor Center said.

"We know this news will be deeply felt by the many thousands of people around the world who have followed her journey, hoped alongside us, prayed for her, and supported the people caring for her.

"We are working closely with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the California Department of Fish and Wildlife and will provide a more comprehensive statement including additional information on her treatments and test results."

Jackie's remains have been transferred to the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, the Ojai Raptor Center said.
body.zh: 杰基是加利福尼亚州的一只秃鹰，后来成为网络明星，在接受了数周的兽医治疗后于周一去世。 杰姬遭到其他鹰的袭击后，由野生动物康复组织奥海猛禽中心负责照顾。这只鸟患有潜在的健康问题，导致贫血和体重减轻。 奥海猛禽中心在一份声明中表示：“在过去的几天里，尽管我们的兽医团队和咨询专家进行了强化治疗，但她的病情仍在继续恶化。” 以 Jackie 和她的伴侣 Shadow 在大熊谷巢穴为主题的直播拥有数十万订阅者。 由加利福尼亚州大熊谷之友非营利组织运营的大熊鹰巢摄像头聚集了一批忠实的追随者，自 2012 年春天孵化以来，杰姬就经常出现在该地区。 大熊谷之友网站称，杰基和影子自 2018 年以来一直是伴侣。 奥海猛禽中心表示：“我们的团队非常伤心。能够照顾她真是一种荣幸。” “我们知道这个消息将被世界各地成千上万的人深深地感受到，他们关注着她的旅程，与我们一起希望，为她祈祷，并支持照顾她的人们。 “我们正在与美国鱼类和野生动物管理局以及加州鱼类和野生动物部门密切合作，并将提供更全面的声明，包括有关她的治疗和测试结果的更多信息。” 奥海猛禽中心表示，杰基的遗体已被转移到加州鱼类和野生动物部门。

reflection.en: The passing of Jackie the eagle, a creature watched and cherished by millions, reminds us of the deep connections we form with the natural world. In moments of loss, even for an animal, we are reminded of the fragility of life and the shared experience of grief that can touch many hearts. Yahweh understands our sorrow, as even Jesus Himself wept in the face...
reflection.zh: 备受数百万人关注和珍爱的白头海雕杰基的离世，提醒我们与自然世界之间深厚的联结。在失去的时刻，即使是对一只动物，我们也想起生命的脆弱和许多人心中共同的悲伤。雅伟理解我们的忧伤，因为即使是耶稣自己也曾为死亡而哭泣。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Turkey MPs back historic law on reintegrating PKK militants
title.zh: 土耳其议员支持关于库尔德工人党武装分子重返社会的历史性法律

summary.en: Turkey's parliament has passed a significant law aimed at ending its four-decade conflict with the PKK. The legislation outlines a framework for some militants to return to civilian life, though the status of Abdullah Ocalan remains unresolved.
summary.zh: 土耳其议会通过了一项具有里程碑意义的法律，旨在结束与库尔德工人党（PKK）长达四十年的冲突。这项新法律规定了部分武装分子如何重返平民生活，但阿卜杜拉·奥贾兰的未来仍未解决。

body.en:
Turkey's parliament has taken a major step toward ending four decades of conflict with the PKK. The new law sets out how some militants can return to civilian life, but leaves Abdullah Ocalan's future unresolved.

Turkey's parliament on Monday approved legislation offering a conditional pardon and legal protections to thousands of members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) .

After around 12 hours of debate, lawmakers voted 468 to 88 in favor of the 12-article bill, with six abstentions. It was backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's AK Party , its nationalist MHP allies and the pro- Kurdish DEM party.

The law sets out procedures for the PKK's disarmament and dissolution and the reintegration of some members into civilian life. The government has stressed that it is not a general amnesty.

Some prison sentences would be suspended, while investigations and trials could be postponed for five or 10 years depending on the offense.

If those covered commit no terrorism-related crime during that period, cases would be dropped and sentences considered served.

Around 3,500 PKK-linked detainees could initially be released, lawmakers said. Media reports suggest exiled members and fighters in Iraq and Syria could also benefit.

People convicted of intentional killings and some serving life sentences are excluded.

The measures will only come into force once Turkey's National Security Council confirms that the PKK has dissolved and surrendered all weapons.

Those seeking to benefit would then have six months to apply. Ministerial and parliamentary committees are also due to monitor the process.

Turkey’s Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz called the vote a "historic step", saying "the 468 'yes' votes are of the utmost importance in terms of political consensus".

The law does not cover imprisoned PKK founder Abdullah Ocalan, 77, who has been held on Imrali island near Istanbul since 1999.

Yilmaz said Ocalan's case "does not fall within the scope of this law", but added that he could remain "in a position to contribute to the peace process".

Ocalan has been central to the initiative. In February 2025, he urged the PKK to disarm and dissolve and pursue Kurdish rights through democratic means.

The PKK announced its dissolution in May 2025. Two months later, militants symbolically burned weapons at a ceremony in northern Iraq and the group said it was withdrawing fighters from Turkey.

The PKK has called the legislation a "beginning" but said it contains "serious shortcomings and deficiencies."

It has demanded Ocalan's release and said the process can move forward only if he "lives and works freely."

title.en: At least 111 people killed after 7.4 magnitude earthquake strikes Colombia
title.zh: 哥伦比亚发生强烈地震，至少111人死亡

summary.en: A powerful earthquake in Colombia's coffee-growing region, particularly the western province of Risaralda, has resulted in the deaths of at least 111 people.

body.en:
Colombia declared a state of emergency overnight following a powerful earthquake that caused at least 111 deaths and flattened dozens of buildings, trapping more victims underneath.

The 7.4-magnitude quake struck western Colombia late on Monday and triggered a frantic search for survivors in several cities.

"The national government is maintaining all its capacities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid to every area that needs it," Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella stated from Bogota.

The leader appointed just three days ago reported 111 deaths, 87 people injured and over 1,000 buildings damaged.

The quake's epicentre was in Colombia's coastal Choco region at a depth of 100km. Authorities in the impoverished area reported 12 deaths.

The nearby city of Pereira was one of the worst-hit areas, with local authorities earlier announcing that at least 40 people had died in the Risaralda region of which it is the provincial capital.

"A great many buildings" in the city sustained damage, administrative worker Jaime Zuluaga, 50, said.

"Traffic is paralysed and people don't want to go back to their homes for fear of an aftershock."

At least 20 buildings crumbled in Colombia's third-largest city, Cali, trapping people beneath the debris, mayor Alejandro Eder said.

Choco's governor warned of serious damage in the provincial capital Quibdo, where videos showed more buildings reduced to rubble.

"We are all devastated," Quibdo community leader Luis Gregorio Moreno told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency.

"At this moment there are reported deaths, dozens of wounded, but what there are most of are missing people," he said.

Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela also felt the early-morning quake, which prompted building evacuations in the Colombian capital, Bogota.

Still wearing their pyjamas, crowds of people rushed out into the street upon feeling the tremor, AFP reporters saw.

"The quake was very, very strong," said content creator Valeria Polo, 29, in the capital, where only minimal damage was recorded.

Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said, and the soccer governing body postponed upcoming football matches.

The United States was "closely monitoring the large earthquake that struck Colombia and stands ready to support the people of Colombia," US secretary of state Marco Rubio said in a post on X.

European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen said the EU was "ready to provide more support" to the South American country.

title.en: The China factor in the United States' $500 million move in a tiny Australian town
title.zh: 中国因素如何影响美国在一个澳大利亚小镇的5亿美元投资

summary.en: The United States is investing $500 million in a small Australian town in New South Wales, a move reportedly influenced by the geopolitical rivalry with China. The Pentagon's sudden interest in this remote location, home to only 130 people, is part of broader strategic considerations.
summary.zh: 美国正在新南威尔士州的一个澳大利亚小镇投资5亿美元，此举据称受到与中国地缘政治竞争的影响。五角大楼对这个仅有130人口的偏远地区突然产生兴趣，是更广泛战略考量的一部分。

body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

summary.zh: 一场里氏7.4级的强烈地震袭击了哥伦比亚，造成超过100人死亡，许多人被困在废墟下。卡利、佩雷拉和马尼萨莱斯等城市受灾严重。

body.zh: 哥伦比亚发生里氏 7.4 级强烈地震，造成数十人死亡，许多人被困在瓦砾下。卡利、佩雷拉和马尼萨莱斯等城市是受灾最严重的城市之一。 地震发生约 6 小时后，哥伦比亚总统表示，全国已确认有 111 人死亡。 卡利和其他城市的建筑物倒塌后，救援队正在努力营救居民。 震中位于哥伦比亚太平洋沿岸乔科省的东端。 哥伦比亚新​​上任总统阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉表示，他亲自负责政府应对紧急情况的工作。 他说，寻找仍然可能被困的人是救援人员的首要任务，并宣布全国进入紧急状态。 德拉埃斯普里埃拉在波哥大表示：“截至（当地时间）12:30，死亡人数为 111 人，受伤人数为 87 人，1,575 所房屋受损，37 所完全被毁，61 栋建筑倒塌，18 所医疗中心和 52 所学校受损。” 欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩表示，欧盟“准备好向哥伦比亚提供更多支持”。该集团的卫星服务“哥白尼”已经动员起来援助救援人员。 “今晚，欧洲的心与哥伦比亚人民同在，”她在社交媒体上写道。 国务卿卢比奥表示，美国正在“密切关注”局势，并随时“准备支持哥伦比亚人民”。 卡利市市长亚历杭德罗·埃德尔表示，至少有 20 座建筑物倒塌，有些建筑物内有人被困。 “卡利的居民们，目前该市至少有 20 处倒塌的建筑物，有人被困在里面；我们已经与卡利的所有救援机构一起应对这一紧急情况，”埃德在 Instagram 上说道，并发布了一段视频声明。 “我已请求波哥大和麦德林市长提供支持，特别是救援人员。” 首府卡利市考卡山谷当局表示，根据总统讲话之前发布的数字，至少有 27 人在地震中丧生。 里萨拉尔达的官员表示，根据市长早些时候的评论，全州已有 40 人死亡，其中至少 18 人在首府佩雷拉。 地震震中所在的乔科地区州长努比亚·卡罗莱纳·科尔多瓦-库里表示，截至当地时间午餐时间，该地区已造成 12 人死亡、84 人受伤。 马尼萨莱斯市市长豪尔赫·爱德华多·罗哈斯在接受电台采访时表示，他的城市位于佩雷拉东北部不远的卡尔达斯地区，有两人被杀。 哥伦比亚民航局报告称，六个相对较小的机场遭到破坏，并表示航班...

reflection.en: In the wake of such a devastating earthquake, communities face immense loss and uncertainty. Psalm 46:1 reminds us that even in the deepest trouble, Yahweh is a present refuge and strength. May those affected find comfort and aid in this time of profound need.
reflection.zh: 在这场毁灭性的地震之后，社区面临着巨大的损失和不确定性。诗篇46:1提醒我们，即使在最深的困境中，雅伟也是我们随时的避难所和力量。愿受影响的人们在这极度需要的时候找到安慰和帮助。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Which country is the new Mecca defense pact targeting?
title.zh: 新的麦加防务协议目标是哪个国家？

summary.en: Observers suggest the new alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan won't result in any of the countries fighting for each other. Instead it's about preventing Iran and Israel from regional dominance, they say.
summary.zh: 观察家们认为，沙特阿拉伯、土耳其和巴基斯坦之间的新联盟不会导致任何国家为彼此而战。相反，他们说，这是为了阻止伊朗和以色列在该地区占据主导地位。

body.en:
Observers suggest the new alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan won't result in any of the countries fighting for each other. Instead it's about preventing Iran and Israel from regional dominance, they say.

Turkey , Pakistan and Saudi Arabia  sealed a historic defense pact on Friday, signing an agreement "intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression."

The so-called "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement" between the three Sunni Muslim-majority states is meant to increase cooperation during regional uncertainty and threats from the Iran war.

The agreement was signed in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan's Prime Minister  Shehbaz Sharif .

The alliance has been likened to a NATO-style alliance and on Friday, the Pakistani foreign ministry said that an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all.

But experts and analysts have been quick to point out that the deal is unlikely to work that way — at least at first.

For example, on the weekend the Houthi rebel group in Yemen fired at Saudi Arabian oil facilities again. The Houthis consider Saudi Arabia their enemy and are also aligned with Iran. The latter has also targeted Saudi Arabia after the US and Israel attacked it, starting a war in late February, because it sees the Saudis as a US ally.

But following the Houthi attack on the weekend, neither Turkey nor Pakistan sprang to the Saudis' defense. Nor are they likely to attack Iran, analysts say. In fact, Pakistan is acting as a mediator between Iran and the US currently.

This arrangement is meant as more of a deterrent and as an "elastic defense pact," Dania Thafer, executive director of the Washington-based think tank the Gulf International Forum, or GIF, told DW late last week.

"If you look at the parties in this agreement, you have Saudi Arabia, which is in the middle of this conflict. But you also have Turkey and Pakistan, who both have relations with Iran and both have relations with the US. So I think it's an extra layer of deterrence, if you will, for Saudi Arabia," Thafer explained. "I think Saudi Arabia is looking at a layered deterrence approach to regional threats as they emerge."

This new alliance is likely to work out in various stages with the short-term goal being a "stabilized region," Kamran Bokhari, a senior fellow at the Middle East Policy Council in Washington, told DW.

Longer term goals will involve defense cooperation rather than fighting, other experts have said.

"The three countries complement each other unusually well," Andreas Krieg, a lecturer in security at King's College London, told news agency Agence France-Presse last week.

title.en: 'Change the game': Ukraine's latest target sits at the centre of everyday Russian life
title.zh: “改变游戏规则”：乌克兰的最新目标位于俄罗斯日常生活的中心

summary.en: Experts note that Ukraine's drone strategy is evolving to target Russia's largest online retailer, indicating a shift in tactics to impact everyday Russian life.
summary.zh: 专家指出，乌克兰的无人机战略正在演变，开始瞄准俄罗斯最大的在线零售商，这表明其战术正在转变，旨在影响俄罗斯民众的日常生活。

body.en:
Ukraine is bringing the war home to Russia, experts say, with a growing campaign of long-range drone strikes targeting infrastructure embedded in everyday Russian life.

More than four years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Ukraine is increasingly using domestically produced drones to strike targets deep inside Russian territory.

Among the targets is Wildberries, Russia's biggest online retailer, with a sprawling network of warehouses and distribution centres.

At least 20 Wildberries locations have been targeted , including sites more than 2,000km from Ukraine.

They say the attacks demonstrate Ukraine's expanding ability to reach deep inside Russia, while making the economic and psychological costs of the war harder for ordinary Russians to ignore.

Professor Matthew Sussex, a defence and national security expert at Deakin University, said Ukraine is deliberately trying to make the war's consequences harder for ordinary Russians to ignore.

"Ukraine is hitting Wildberries mainly to bring the cost of war home to Russians," he said.

He described Wildberries as Russia's version of Amazon, a platform where people can buy almost anything and have it delivered to their door.

"Wildberries has become extremely popular for everyday Russians to order things, consumer goods that they have relied on in the past which have become unavailable due to the sanctions regime [placed on Russia by other countries]," he said.

Sussex said Ukraine's strategy is ultimately about making Russians feel the consequences of a war that, for many, has remained at a distance.

"If you're in Moscow or some parts of St Petersburg, you don't really feel the cost of the conflict," he said.

Ukraine says Wildberries has been involved in supplying Russian forces with military and dual-use equipment.

Retired Australian Army major-general Mick Ryan agreed there's a strategic reason for choosing Wildberries.

"These things are part of the Russian military logistics network," he said. "Russian soldiers and units buy things out of these warehouses all the time."

Wildberries and the Russian government have both said the e-commerce giant does not supply to the army.

Sussex believes the broader economic impact is ultimately more significant. Wildberries has billions of dollars in annual sales, and thousands of Russian businesses rely on the platform to sell and distribute their products.

"The concern is that if these attacks continue, then Wildberries may have to be bailed out by the government," Sussex said.

title.en: The tiny island bracing for an Odyssey tourism boom — even though it wasn't in the film
title.zh: 小岛为“奥德赛”旅游热潮做准备，尽管它并未出现在电影中

summary.en: Locals on a small island anticipate a significant increase in tourism, driven by the mistaken belief that the island was featured in a popular film. However, some residents express disappointment that no scenes were actually filmed there.
summary.zh: 一个小岛的居民预计旅游业将大幅增长，因为人们误以为该岛曾出现在一部热门电影中。然而，一些居民对岛上并未拍摄任何场景感到失望。

body.en:
Standing on the ferry as it waits to dock on the Greek island of Ithaca, Giorgia Ongarato is only too keen to talk about the Odyssey — the epic poem that inspired Christopher Nolan's blockbuster film.

The Italian lawyer said it was her dream to come to Ithaca, widely believed to be the same island the poem's hero Odysseus called home.

Dressed in a T-shirt emblazoned with the word 'Odyssey' in ancient Greek alongside a line from the poem, she enthused: "I studied Greek when I was a child, and I studied the Odyssey."

While she stressed that the film was not her entry point into the tale of the hero battling his way back home from the Trojan war, the 50-year-old said she was also a fan of the film — describing it as "wonderful".

The island's businesses and officials now expect the film to inspire many more to follow in her footsteps.

Ithaca, in the Ionian Sea off the west coast of mainland Greece, is far from the country's tourist hubs, and despite crystal-clear waters and spectacular bays, it has never been a regular stop for travellers.

Its interior is rugged, carpeted with olive and cypress trees, and strikingly calm even at the height of the tourist season.

Although the movie has undoubtedly piqued the interest of many, it has also been slightly controversial in Greece — although some Greek locations were used, not a single scene in the blockbuster was shot on Ithaca.

That decision has upset some on the island of roughly 3,000 inhabitants, where the film has been shown twice in open-air screenings since its 16 July worldwide release.

Xhimi Xoxha, who runs a restaurant in Ithaca's capital of Vathi, said he was content that the movie was already "generating publicity for the island". He predicted the positive effects would continue.

While Ithaca mayor Dionysis Stanitsas agreed that the publicity was "tremendous", he could not hide his disappointment that the island itself did not feature.

"We had reached out to the production team and asked that some scenes be filmed here on the island," he said. "Unfortunately, that wasn't feasible."

He is, however, counting on rising demand next year, and the island was already fully booked for this season by the time the film came out.

"As more people see it, they will begin planning trips to visit the island," he said.

Visitors will not find a palace of Odysseus or any spectacular archaeological site likely to confirm the existence of the hero of Homer's poem.

But village squares and the town hall are dotted with statues of Odysseus and Homer.

body.zh: 乔治亚·翁加拉托 (Giorgia Ongarato) 站在等待停靠希腊伊萨卡岛的渡轮上，非常热衷于谈论《奥德赛》——这首史诗为克里斯托弗·诺兰 (Christopher Nolan) 的大片提供了灵感。 这位意大利律师说，她的梦想是来到伊萨卡岛，人们普遍认为，这里就是诗中英雄奥德修斯的家乡。 她穿着一件印有古希腊语“奥德赛”一词以及这首诗中的一句的T恤，她热情地说：“我小时候学过希腊语，也研究过《奥德赛》。” 虽然她强调，这部电影并不是她讲述英雄从特洛伊战争中奋战回家的故事的切入点，但这位 50 岁的女士表示，她也是这部电影的粉丝，称其“精彩”。 岛上的企业和官员现在期望这部电影能够激励更多人追随她的脚步。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 伊萨卡位于希腊大陆西海岸的爱奥尼亚海，远离该国的旅游中心，尽管拥有清澈的海水和壮观的海湾，但它从来都不是游客的常规停留地。 它的内部崎岖不平，铺满了橄榄树和柏树，即使在旅游旺季也显得异常平静。 尽管这部电影无疑激起了很多人的兴趣，但它在希腊也引起了一些争议——尽管使用了一些希腊外景地，但大片中没有一个场景是在伊萨卡岛拍摄的。 这一决定让岛上大约 3,000 名居民感到不安，自 7 月 16 日在全球上映以来，这部电影已在岛上露天放映了两次。 在伊萨卡岛首府瓦西经营一家餐厅的希米·索克哈 (Xhimi Xoxha) 表示，他对这部电影已经“为该岛进行宣传”感到满意。他预计积极影响将持续下去。 虽然伊萨卡岛市长迪奥尼西斯·斯坦尼察斯（Dionysis Stanitsas）也认为宣传效果“巨大”，但他无法掩饰对该岛本身没有出现的失望。 “我们已经联系了制作团队，要求在岛上拍摄一些场景，”他说。 “不幸的是，这是不可行的。” 然而，他预计明年的需求会不断增长，而在电影上映时，该岛本季的预订已满。 “随着越来越多的人看到它，他们将开始计划参观该岛的旅行，”他说。 游客不会发现奥德修斯的宫殿或任何可能证实荷马史诗中英雄存在的壮观的考古遗址。 但村庄广场和市政厅点缀着奥德修斯和荷马的雕像。 在阳光普照的小港口，船只在碧绿的海水中摇曳，船只的名字如忒勒马科斯（……的儿子）。

reflection.en: This story reminds us that external validation, like the praise or attention an island receives, can test our true values. While a tourism boom is welcome, the disappointment over not being genuinely featured in the film reveals a deeper longing for authentic recognition. Yahweh invites us to find our worth not in fleeting fame, but in the enduring purpose...
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，外部的认可，例如一个岛屿所受到的赞扬或关注，可以考验我们真正的价值观。虽然旅游业的繁荣是受欢迎的，但对未能真正出现在电影中感到失望，揭示了对真实认可的更深层渴望。雅伟邀请我们不要在短暂的名声中寻找价值，而要在祂为我们预备的永恒目的中找到。

verse.textZh: 鼎为炼银，炉为炼金，人的称赞也试炼人。

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin: Beijing braces for one-third of its annual rainfall as storm sweeps China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”：风暴席卷中国，北京严阵以待，预计将迎来年降雨量三分之一的降水

summary.en: Over a million people were evacuated across eastern China as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall, with Beijing anticipating over a third of its annual rainfall within a 24-hour period starting late Tuesday.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”登陆中国东部，导致逾百万民众被转移至安全地带。北京预计将从周二晚些时候开始的24小时内，迎来超过其年降雨量三分之一的降水。

body.en: More than a million people were moved to safety across eastern China over the weekend as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall Beijing is expected to hit by more than one-third of its annual rainfall over a ⁠24 hour period starting late Tuesday, as Typhoon Dolphin moves deeper ⁠inland prompting the closure of tourist areas and suspension of construction projects. From ‌Tuesday evening through to Thursday, most areas in Beijing will experience heavy ‌downpours with a cumulative rainfall of more than 150mm in 24 hours, the city’s meteorological service has forecast. That compares with Beijing’s average annual rainfall of 528mm, the bulk of which normally falls between June and September. Continue reading...
body.zh: 周末，台风“海豚”登陆中国东部地区，超过一百万人被转移至安全地带，预计从周二晚间开始，北京将在 24 小时内遭遇年降雨量的三分之一以上，因为台风“海豚”向内陆深处移动，导致旅游区关闭和建设项目暂停。据北京市气象部门预报，周二晚至周四，北京大部分地区将出现大暴雨，24小时内累计降雨量将超过150毫米。相比之下，北京的年平均降雨量为 528 毫米，其中大部分通常发生在 6 月至 9 月之间。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As communities brace for the impact of Typhoon Dolphin and millions seek safety, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble. In the face of overwhelming natural forces, we are called to remember that even amidst the storm, there is a source of unwavering support and protection.

title.en: Why did Saudi Arabia just spend billions on a video games company? – podcast
title.zh: 沙特阿拉伯为何斥巨资收购一家视频游戏公司？——播客

summary.en: Saudi Arabia's wealth fund and a group of investors recently spent $55 billion to acquire Electronic Arts, a major video game company. This significant investment is viewed as a soft-power move and has generated considerable concern within the industry.
summary.zh: 沙特阿拉伯主权财富基金及投资者近期斥资550亿美元收购了大型视频游戏公司艺电。这一重大投资被视为一项软实力举措，并引发了业内许多人的担忧。

body.en: Last week Saudi Arabia’s wealth fund and a group of investors spent $55bn (£41bn) on Electronic Arts, the video games company behind the Sims, Madden NFL and Battlefield. Keith Stuart and George Osborn tell Annie Kelly why this soft-power move is worrying many in the industry Saudi Arabia’s crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, loves a video game. That might explain why Saudi Arabia has borrowed billions to buy Electronic Arts. And that’s just the latest in a long list of ways the Middle Eastern powerhouse has invested in esports. But why would such a powerful government take a risk with video games? As Keith Stuart and George Osborn tell Annie Kelly, it’s part of a pattern of superpowers and authoritarian regimes seeing games as handy propaganda tools. And this is why critics are worried about countries such as Saudi Arabia having ready access to billions of players around the world Continue reading...

reflection.en: Large-scale investments, like the recent acquisition of a major video game company, highlight the immense power of wealth in shaping industries and influence. While capital can fuel innovation, the biblical warning reminds us that when the pursuit of money becomes an ultimate goal, it can lead to unforeseen ethical challenges and widespread concern.
reflection.zh: 像近期收购一家大型视频游戏公司这样的大规模投资，凸显了财富在塑造行业和影响力方面的巨大力量。虽然资本可以促进创新，但圣经的警告提醒我们，当对金钱的追求成为最终目标时，它可能导致意想不到的伦理挑战和普遍的担忧。

title.en: The lonely Chinese men being conned by fake brides
title.zh: 孤独的中国男性被假新娘诈骗

summary.en: "Flash marriage" scams are an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis long in the making in China.
summary.zh: “闪婚”骗局是中国长期存在的人口危机的一个极端症状。

body.en:
At 37, Wang Zhuang had almost given up hope of finding a wife, until he saw the glossy matchmaking adverts.

They promised he wouldn't have to waste years on building a relationship that had no future. They offered to introduce him to a demure, devoted woman.

"The matchmakers said that girls from Guizhou are frugal," Wang says. "They told me they are good at running a household, able to do housework, and their families are very poor, so after marrying into your family, they would settle down and live a life with you."

So Wang travelled to Guiyang, a city in the southwestern province of Guizhou, in the hope of finding his soulmate.

He thought he had, when he was matched with a woman who seemed to tick every box. They had only met a few times before they married.

He is still picking up the pieces more than a year after he discovered that everything he had been told by his wife was a lie.

She was a former karaoke hostess who'd been married three times, had three children, a serious sexually transmitted disease and was deeply in debt. She had even lied about her age.

He is fighting for a divorce and cannot return home to his old life - at least until he can recoup some of his life savings, which he says he paid to the agency within hours of being introduced to several potential matches.

Wang's story is an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis that has long been in the making in China.

For decades, China's Communist Party decreed that couples could have only one child. They reversed course in January 2016 but by then the "one-child" policy, coupled with a preference for boys, had produced a shrinking pool of women and a stark gender imbalance.

There are now 30 million more men than women in China – that's more than the male population of the UK, or the entire population of Australia.

This has left men like Wang, who are in their late 30s and who live in smaller cities or far-flung, rural areas, with few options. Women in these places can afford to be choosy as they know they are in demand.

"The requirements for men are very high in my city. You need to have a car, a house and your family should preferably run a business," he says.

Many families also demand a high "bride price", a longstanding Chinese custom where the groom's family gives money to the bride. In parts of China, where men far outnumber women, this has become a significant financial burden.

Hence the appeal of matchmaking agencies like the ones in Guizhou, which are proposing a one-stop, quick solution - or "flash marriages".

Matchmaking agencies are hardly new in China, but many seem to be finding vulnerable targets in men who are struggling to find partners as they grow older.

body.zh: 37岁的王壮几乎放弃了找老婆的希望，直到他看到了光鲜亮丽的婚介广告。 他们承诺他不必浪费数年时间来建立一种没有未来的关系。他们提出要向他介绍一位端庄、忠诚的女士。 “媒人说贵州姑娘很节俭，”王说。 “他们告诉我，他们很会持家，会做家务，而且家里很穷，所以嫁入你家后，就会安定下来，和你一起生活。” 于是，王先生前往西南部贵州省贵阳市，希望找到他的灵魂伴侣。 当他与一个似乎符合所有条件的女人相匹配时，他认为他已经做到了。他们在结婚前只见过几次面。 一年多后，他发现妻子告诉他的一切都是谎言，现在仍在收拾残局。 她曾是一名卡拉 OK 女主持人，结过三次婚，育有三个孩子，患有严重的性病，负债累累。她甚至谎报了自己的年龄。 他正在为离婚而奋斗，无法回家过往的生活——至少在他能收回部分毕生积蓄之前是这样。他说，在被介绍给几位潜在的匹配对象后，他在几个小时内就将这笔钱付给了该机构。 王的故事是中国长期存在的人口危机的一个极端症状。 几十年来，中国共产党规定一对夫妇只能生育一个孩子。 2016 年 1 月，他们改变了做法，但当时的“独生子女”政策，加上重男轻女，导致女性人数不断减少，性别比例明显失衡。 现在中国的男性比女性多3000万——这比英国的男性人口或澳大利亚的总人口还要多。 这使得像王这样30多岁、生活在小城市或偏远农村地区的男性几乎没有选择。这些地方的女性可以做出挑剔，因为她们知道自己很受欢迎。 “我的城市对男性的要求非常高。你需要有车、有房子，而且你的家人最好应该经营一家企业，”他说。 许多家庭还要求高额“彩礼”，这是中国由来已久的习俗，即新郎的家人给新娘钱。在中国部分地区，男性人数远多于女性，这已成为沉重的经济负担。 因此，像贵州这样的婚介机构提出了一站式、快速的解决方案，即“闪婚”。 婚介机构在中国并不新鲜，但许多机构似乎都在寻找随着年龄增长而难以寻找伴侣的男性这一弱势目标。 以至于官方媒体最近报道称该行业已经“快速增长”，这......

This reminds us of the wisdom in Proverbs 14:15, which encourages careful discernment rather than naive belief. In a world where trust can be exploited, Yahweh calls us to seek wisdom and protect the...
reflection.zh: “闪婚”骗局凸显了那些寻求伴侣之人的痛苦脆弱，他们在孤独中可能变得容易受骗。这让我们想起箴言14:15的智慧，它鼓励我们仔细辨别，而不是天真地相信一切。在一个信任可能被利用的世界里，雅伟呼召我们寻求智慧，保护弱势群体免受欺骗。

title.en: The China factor in the United States' $500 million move in a tiny Australian town
title.zh: 美国在澳大利亚小镇投资5亿美元的“中国因素”

summary.en: The Pentagon is investing $500 million in a small Australian town in New South Wales, sparking questions about China's role in this strategic move. The sudden interest in a town of only 130 people highlights the geopolitical competition between the United States and China.
summary.zh: 五角大楼正在澳大利亚新南威尔士州的一个小镇投资5亿美元，引发了人们对中国在此次战略行动中所扮演角色的疑问。对一个仅有130人的小镇突然产生兴趣，凸显了美国和中国之间的地缘政治竞争。

body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

title.en: Weather tracker: Europe breaks more heat records as temperatures soar
title.zh: 天气追踪：欧洲气温飙升打破更多高温纪录

summary.en: Europe is experiencing record-breaking heat, leading to intensifying drought and wildfires across the continent. Meanwhile, tropical storms are causing heavy rain and disruption in East Asia.
summary.zh: 欧洲多地气温飙升，打破了多项高温纪录，导致整个大陆的干旱和野火加剧。与此同时，热带风暴给东亚带来了强降雨和混乱。

body.en: Drought and wildfires intensify across continent, while tropical storms bring heavy rain and disruption to east Asia High pressure has dominated central and eastern Europe in early August, breaking temperature records across the region. Austria recorded a high of 41.2C (106.2F), while Slovakia reached 42.2C. Hungary hit a peak of 41.8C, surpassing a record set in 1905, while overnight temperatures remained above 28C in some areas, marking it as a tropical night. The extreme temperatures have been driven by a heat dome beneath the high-pressure system, which traps warm air close to the surface. Continue reading...
body.zh: 整个大陆的干旱和野火加剧，热带风暴给东亚带来大雨和破坏。8月初，高压主导了中欧和东欧，打破了该地区的气温记录。奥地利的最高气温达到 41.2 摄氏度（106.2 华氏度），而斯洛伐克则达到 42.2 摄氏度。匈牙利的最高气温达到41.8摄氏度，超过了1905年创下的纪录，而部分地区夜间气温仍保持在28摄氏度以上，标志着热带之夜。极端温度是由高压系统下方的热穹造成的，该热穹将暖空气困在靠近地表的地方。继续阅读...

title.en: China: Typhoon Dolphin prompts mass evacuation, canceled flights
title.zh: 中国：台风海豚引发大规模疏散，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin is causing significant disruption across China, leading to the cancellation of nearly 1,500 flights in Shanghai and flood alerts in parts of Beijing, even as the storm begins to weaken.
summary.zh: 台风海豚正在中国各地造成严重破坏，尽管风力减弱，上海仍有近1500个航班被取消，北京部分地区也发布了洪水警报。

body.en:
Even as it weakens, Typhoon Dolphin is disrupting life in China. Close to 1,500 flights have been canceled in Shanghai while parts of Beijing are under flood alert.

Heavy rainfall and strong winds prompted flood alerts and more than 1,000 flight cancellations across China on Monday, even as Typhoon Dolphin weakened.

China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issued its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning as the storm lost power after making landfall in China's Zhejiang Province on Sunday.

Despite the weaker storm, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China will continue to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities issued their most severe flash flood alert for parts of eastern and southern Zhejiang on Monday, state news broadcaster CCTV reported. 

Five districts in Beijing are also under red alerts for heavy rainfall on Monday, with risks of landslides and flooding.

The storm had already forced over 300,000 people in eastern China to preemptively relocate, while bringing heavy rainfall to northern Taiwan over the weekend. In Shanghai, authorities evacuated more than 30,000 people out of high-risk areas. Overall, some one million people have been told to seek shelter. 

Shanghai's two main passenger airports, Pudong International Airport and Hongqiao International Airport, canceled 943 flights between them for Monday, the airport authority said in a post online. That's a reduction of capacity by nearly 40%.

On Sunday, the two airports had cancelled nearly 1,500 flights, or about 60% of their scheduled travel, according to state media.

Public transport services in the city were also impacted, with several local trains suspended.

Zhejiang's Ningbo International Airport will resume flights midday on Monday but warned that some of the scheduled travel may still be delayed or canceled as the storm had "not yet completely dissipated."

China is dealing with Typhoon Dolphin just two weeks after Typhoon Noul struck its southern Guangdong province. Last month, Typhoon Maysak killed 11 people and injured over 300 in the central Hubei province.

Extreme weather systems are a common feature in China this time of the year, with typhoons leaving significant displacement , infrastructural damage and loss of lives. Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of such extreme weather have increased and will continue to rise amid climate change.

body.zh: 尽管海豚台风强度减弱，但它仍在扰乱中国的生活。上海近 1,500 个航班已取消，北京部分地区处于洪水警报状态。 尽管台风“海豚”强度减弱，但周一，强降雨和强风导致中国各地发布洪水警报，并导致 1,000 多个航班取消。 中国国家气象中心（NMC）周一早上发布了最轻的台风警报，风暴周日在中国浙江省登陆后失去了动力。 尽管风暴强度减弱，但国家气象局警告说，华东和中部部分地区将继续遭遇强降雨。据官方新闻媒体中央电视台报道，当局周一对浙江东部和南部部分地区发布了最严重的山洪警报。 周一，北京五个区也进入强降雨红色预警，存在山体滑坡和洪水风险。 这场风暴已经迫使中国东部地区超过30万人提前搬迁，同时周末给台湾北部带来了强降雨。在上海，当局从高风险地区疏散了3万多人。总体而言，约有一百万人被告知寻求庇护。 机场管理局在网上发布消息称，上海两大客运机场浦东国际机场和虹桥国际机场周一取消了943个往返航班。这意味着容量减少了近 40%。 据官方媒体报道，周日，这两个机场取消了近 1,500 个航班，约占预定航班的 60%。 该市的公共交通服务也受到影响，多趟当地列车停运。 浙江宁波国际机场将于周一中午恢复航班，但警告称，由于风暴“尚未完全消散”，部分原定航班可能仍会被推迟或取消。 台风“诺尔”袭击广东省南部两周后，中国正在应对台风“海豚”。上个月，台风美莎克在湖北省中部造成11人死亡、300多人受伤。 每年这个时候，极端天气系统是中国的一个常见特征，台风造成大量人员流离失所、基础设施损坏和人员伤亡。科学家警告说，随着气候变化，这种极端天气的强度和频率已经增加，并将继续增加。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

Yahweh's word in Romans 8:22 speaks to this, noting that all creation groans as it awaits redemption. Even amidst the challenges, we can hold onto hope for a future where all things are made new.

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

Fletcher was Australia's ambassador to China from 2019 to 2023 and led the negotiating team in 2014 that helped seal a free trade agreement between the two...
body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

reflection.en: When nations face a "gulf" in worldviews, the path to peace can seem daunting. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace actively, recognizing that while complete agreement may not always be possible, our commitment to peaceful coexistence remains vital. This calls for wisdom and perseverance in navigating complex international relations.
reflection.zh: 当国家之间面临“世界观鸿沟”时，通往和平的道路可能显得令人生畏。雅伟的话语鼓励我们积极寻求和平，认识到虽然完全一致可能并非总是可行，但我们对和平共处的承诺至关重要。这要求我们在复杂的国际关系中运用智慧和毅力。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

Australia's cash rate remains higher than those of several comparable economies after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) left it unchanged at 4.35 per cent on Tuesday.

The decision underscores a key difference between Australia and many of its peers: inflation has proved more persistent, prompting the central bank to take a more cautious approach to cutting rates.

In its statement of monetary policy, the board explained its widely-anticipated decision was affected by global uncertainty and high inflation in 2026.

"The board remains focused on ensuring that high inflation does not become embedded," it said in its board statement announcing the decision to leave the cash rate on hold.

"While the impact of the Middle East conflict on inflation has so far been less than expected, headline inflation is still too high."

The latest inflation data showed signs of cooling but it is still running about the RBA's 2-3 per cent target band, and the ongoing global uncertainty is likely to give the central bank "reason to pause", according to AMP chief economist Shane Oliver.

Oliver described interest rates as a "blunt instrument" for central banks around the world to reduce households' spending on discretionary items and tackle inflation.

Oliver explained that, historically, levers reserve banks can pull have been the best way to tackle inflation.

Relying on governments alone to help doesn't work as well, he said, because governments can be incentivised to spend more to win votes, even when inflation is high.

Cash rate targets differ around the world but share the unifying goal of keeping inflation down and promoting a high-employment economy.

Australia's cash rate target of 4.35 per cent is higher than those of other countries, such as the United States at 3.5-3.75 per cent, the UK at 3.75 per cent, and Canada at 2.25 per cent.

Australia also has higher core inflation, a measure stripping out economic volatility, than these other economies.

Professor and economist Warwick McKibbin from the Australian National University said that trends such as oil supply shocks can impact inflation globally.

Domestic factors, such as economic structure and openness to trade, can also play a part.

"The US has an inflation target of 2 per cent, that's the Federal Reserve's goal," McKibbin said.

"And so, historically, inflation generally doesn't rise significantly above that, although it actually has since COVID-19."

While it was an expected move, there are still risks for the board to navigate. Here are the key takeaways from today's decision:

Compare the Market’s economic director David Koch said the hold is the "right decision" as Australians deal with "a lot of stress out there".

"Inflation is still rising at a greater rate than the Reserve Bank would like, but it’s being driven by factors beyond the control of Australian households, who are still facing a massive cost-of-living crisis," he said in a statement.

"And then you layer on that, their biggest asset — property prices — are recently starting to come down and there’s a lot of stress out there."

KPMG Australia chief economist Brendan Rynne said that drops in property prices could also reduce inflation.

"It certainly going to help, because there's an idea of the wealth effect — as we feel like our house[s] are starting to decline that we feel less wealthy and consume less," he told ABC News Channel.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers says the interest rate hold is positive news but has acknowledged there's "more work to do".

"This will come as a relief to Australians with a mortgage," he said in a post on social media after the decision was announced.

"It’s a welcome decision at a time of heightened uncertainty in the world and persistent pressures at home.

"We've made progress on inflation and in the economy, but there's more work to do because people are still under pressure."

The RBA board has also weighed in on other financial conditions, beyond inflation, that contributed to its decision.

It noted that consumer spending growth is gradually slowing "as expected", while growth in business debt and investment remains strong.

"Momentum in the housing market has shifted, with housing prices falling in some capital cities and new housing loans declining noticeably," its statement on monetary policy reads.

"Labour market conditions have eased by a little more than expected in recent months. Labour market leading indicators point to only limited easing in the near term."

The RBA board predicts that inflation will remain above 2.5 per cent — the midpoint of its 2-3 per cent target range — until mid-2027.

"There continue to be heightened uncertainties about the outlook for domestic economic activity and inflation," it said in its decision statement.
